intro: The Hodgkin Lymphoma — Ann Arbor Stage is a oncology scoring tool used in paediatric practice. Ann Arbor staging (Toronto Tier 1) with Cotswolds modification. It scores 1 criteria and interprets the total across 4 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in oncology
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 1 criteria: Extent of disease. Totals are then banded: 1 stage or more - Stage I: stage I - limited disease. Usually low-risk therapy: short chemotherapy ± involved-site radiotherapy; 2 stage or more - Stage II: stage II - favourable or unfavourable depending on bulk and B symptoms; therapy is response-adapted; 3 stage or more - Stage III: stage III - advanced disease. Multi-agent chemotherapy with response-adapted radiotherapy; 4 stage or more - Stage IV: stage IV - disseminated. High-risk multi-agent chemotherapy; consider CHIPS for prognostication.
guidelineRefs: Suffix A = no systemic symptoms; B = fever >38 °C, drenching night sweats, or >10% weight loss in 6 months. Suffix E = limited contiguous extranodal extension; X = bulky disease.
Source: Gupta S, Aitken JF, Bartels U et al. Paediatric cancer stage in population-based cancer registries: the Toronto consensus principles and guidelines. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:e163-72.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the Hodgkin Lymphoma — Ann Arbor Stage use?
What do the bands of the Hodgkin Lymphoma — Ann Arbor Stage mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: 1 stage or more - Stage I: stage I - limited disease. Usually low-risk therapy: short chemotherapy ± involved-site radiotherapy; 2 stage or more - Stage II: stage II - favourable or unfavourable depending on bulk and B symptoms; therapy is response-adapted; 3 stage or more - Stage III: stage III - advanced disease. Multi-agent chemotherapy with response-adapted radiotherapy; 4 stage or more - Stage IV: stage IV - disseminated. High-risk multi-agent chemotherapy; consider CHIPS for prognostication.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.
